newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Central Bank not to change forex policy.
newsitem.headline: Russian Central Bank not to change forex policy.

text.p: The Central Bank of Russia sees no reason for a change soon in its currency policy, which provides for a steady depreciation of the rouble, a bank spokesman quoted Chairman Sergei Dubinin as saying.
Dubinin said at a meeting with Deutsche Bank officials Wednesday that domestic inflation would inevitably lead to a depreciation of the rouble against the dollar.
A rise in the rouble would not be welcome as it would hurt exporters, the spokesman quoted him as saying.

The Central Bank keeps the rouble/dollar rate in a currency band, known here as a sloping corridor, which allows businesses to predict the exchange rate over several months and provides stability in decision-making.
First introduced in mid-1995, the 1997 band envisages a rouble range of 5,750-6,350 to the dollar by the end of the year, compared with 5,500-6,100 at the start of the year.
Within these daily ranges the Central Bank sets separate bid and offer rates for its own operations.
The rouble has never strayed from within the corridor, or from the central bank's own intervention rates within this.
Dubinin said the Central Bank had been buying hard currency on the interbank market during the last six weeks and its net international reserves had risen by 50 percent since the start of the year.
At the beginning of March net currency reserves were worth 6.6 trillion roubles .
